citations.quote:
Fix gravity $g>0$ and a stationary bed $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$. A shallow-water state is a pair $U=(h,m)$ with depth $h\ge0$ and momentum $m\in\mathbb R$. Its admissible wet/dry state set is
$$K=\{(h,m):h>0,\ m\in\mathbb R\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.$$
For $U\in K$, define velocity by $u=m/h$ when $h>0$ and $u=0$ when $h=0$. Thus a dry state has both $h=0$ and $m=0$. Define the free surface by $\eta=h+b$ and the physical flux by
$$F(U)=\begin{cases}(m,\ m^2/h+gh^2/2),&h>0,\\(0,0),&U=(0,0).\end{cases}$$
For a continuously differentiable bed, the one-dimensional shallow-water balance law is
$$U_t+\partial_xF(U)=(0,-gh\,b_x).$$
The source is evaluated as zero at a dry state.

A discrete lake-at-rest profile with level $\eta_0$ has $m_i=0$ and $h_i+b_i=\eta_0$ in every wet cell; cells with $h_i=0$ are dry and satisfy $b_i\ge\eta_0$.

derivations.claim: Write $r_-:=\max(-r,0)$. On each compact rectangle $Q\subset\mathbb R\times(0,T)$, $h_k\ge0$ implies $h_-\le|h-h_k|$, so $\int_Qh_-\le\|h-h_k\|_{L^1(Q)}\to0$. On each compact interval $I\subset\mathbb R$, $h_k^0\ge0$ gives $(h_0)_-\le|h_0-h_k^0|$, so $\int_I(h_0)_-\le\|h_0-h_k^0\|_{L^1(I)}\to0$. Countable compact exhaustions of $\mathbb R\times(0,T)$ and $\mathbb R$ now give $h\ge0$ and $h_0\ge0$ almost everywhere on their domains.

Where $h>0$, [F1] allows arbitrary momentum $m$; where $h=0$, $m=hu=0$, so $U\in K$. For the initial data, on each compact interval $I$ the bound on $u_k^0$ and $U_k^0\in K$ imply $|m_k^0|\le M_Ih_k^0$. Hence $(|m_0|-M_Ih_0)_+\le |m_0-m_k^0|+M_I|h_k^0-h_0|$ pointwise, and integration followed by strong $L^1(I)$ convergence gives $|m_0|\le M_Ih_0$ almost everywhere. Thus $m_0=0$ wherever $h_0=0$; step 1.1 gives $h_0\ge0$, and [F1] yields $U_0\in K$. A countable compact exhaustion proves the bulk and initial claims almost everywhere on their domains.

derivations.claim: Suppose $h_R^*=0$. Then $u_R^*=c_R^*=0$. If both speeds are zero, [F1] makes the full flux zero. If $a_L<0=a_R$, the second branch is $F_R^*=(0,0)$. derivations.claim: Fix a face and set $b^*=\max(b_L,b_R)$. If a side cell is wet, its free surface is $\eta_0$, so its reconstructed depth is $(\eta_0-b^*)_+$. If a side cell is dry, then $b_s\ge\eta_0$ and $b^*\ge b_s$, so its reconstructed depth is $(b_s-b^*)_+=0=(\eta_0-b^*)_+$. Thus both reconstructed depths equal $H=(\eta_0-b^*)_+$, and both reconstructed velocities are zero.

If $H>0$, the states on the face are equal to $(H,0)$ and the middle HLL formula has speeds $-\sqrt{gH}$ and $\sqrt{gH}$, so its flux is $F(H,0)=(0,gH^2/2)$. If $H=0$, both states and speeds are zero and the dry branch returns $(0,0)$. Thus in either case the common flux is $(0,gH^2/2)$.

On the side belonging to a cell of depth $h_s$, the correction in [F2] changes this common flux to $(0,g h_s^2/2)$. Therefore the right corrected flux of cell $i$ and the left corrected flux of that same cell are both $(0,g h_i^2/2)$. Their difference is zero, so the update leaves every $U_i$ unchanged.

derivations.claim: Write $p_R$ for the left-state coefficient at face $i+1/2$, $q_L$ for the right-state coefficient at face $i-1/2$, and use analogous notation for the two inflow coefficients. Expanding the first component of [F1] with [F2] gives $h_i^{n+1}=h_i^n-\lambda(p_R h_{i,+}^*+q_L h_{i,-}^*)+\lambda(q_R h_{i+1,-}^*+p_L h_{i-1,+}^*)$. The inflow terms are nonnegative and the total outflow is at most $(a_{R,i+1/2}-a_{L,i-1/2})h_i^n$, so the CFL gives $h_i^{n+1}\ge0$.

If $h_i^n>0$ and at least one outgoing speed is positive, the corresponding outflow term is strictly below its speed bound times $h_i^n$: this follows from [F2] if the reconstructed depth is positive, and is immediate if that reconstructed depth is zero. By step 1.1 and the CFL, $h_i^{n+1}>0$. If both outgoing speeds are zero, the outflow is zero and step 1.1 gives $h_i^{n+1}\ge h_i^n>0$. Thus a wet cell remains wet.

If $h_i^n=0$, then $m_i^n=0$ and [F1] gives $h_{i,+}^*=h_{i,-}^*=0$, so both corrections on this cell vanish. Its left face has dry right state and its right face has dry left state. By [F3], the left mass flux is nonnegative and the right mass flux nonpositive; if the updated depth is zero, nonnegativity forces both mass fluxes to vanish.

In the zero-depth case of step 2.2, [F3] makes both full HLL face fluxes zero. The cell corrections also vanish, so its updated momentum is zero. If instead its updated depth is positive, its updated state lies in $K$ by [F1]. Together with step 2.1, every updated state lies in $K$; [F4] and [F5] therefore make $K$ a convex invariant domain for this specified one-step map.

Multiplying the first component of each update by $\Delta x$ and summing over the finite chain cancels every interior shared mass flux, because the one-sided corrections have zero first component. This gives $\Delta x\sum_{i=1}^N(h_i^{n+1}-h_i^n)=-\Delta t(\widehat F^h_{N+1/2}-\widehat F^h_{1/2})$. Thus only boundary discharge changes finite-domain water; periodic identification makes the right-hand side zero. Combining this identity with steps 2.1 and 3.1 proves the theorem.

derivations.claim: Put $a=b'(x_i)d$. Taylor's formula gives $b(x_i+d)-b(x_i)=a+r_+$ and $b(x_i-d)-b(x_i)=-a+r_-$ with $|r_\pm|\le C_0d^2$ on the compact interval. Since $s\mapsto s_+$ is $1$-Lipschitz and $a_+-(-a)_+=a$, it follows that $\delta_{i,+}-\delta_{i,-}=b'(x_i)d+O(d^2)$, with a uniform remainder.

For $h\ge0$ and $\delta\ge0$, write $(h-\delta)_+^2=h^2-2h\delta+R(h,\delta)$. If $\delta\le h$, then $R=\delta^2$; if $\delta>h$, then $R=2h\delta-h^2$, which lies between $0$ and $\delta^2$ because $\delta^2-(2h\delta-h^2)=(\delta-h)^2$. Also $\delta_{i,\pm}=O(d)$ uniformly, so [F1] and step 1.1 give $(S_i^n)_2=-g h_i^n b'(x_i)+O(d)$ uniformly for $0\le h_i^n\le H$.

On each cell, $|b'(x)-b'(x_i)|\le \|b''\|_\infty d/2$. Thus the piecewise-constant source differs from $(0,-g h_d b'(x))$ by at most $C_1d$ on compact space-time cylinders. Strong local $L^1$ convergence of $h_d$ then gives strong local $L^1$ convergence of the source to $(0,-ghb')$, as asserted in [F2].

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice.

Let $1 \le p < \infty$ and $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$. Then

$$\|\tau_h f-f\|_p \longrightarrow 0 \qquad(h \to 0).$$

Let $n \ge 1$ and **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]). Then:

1. $\lambda_n$ is sigma-finite ([[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]):
   the cubes $(-k,k]^n$ are Lebesgue measurable with
   $\lambda_n\big((-k,k]^n\big) = (2k)^n < +\infty$, they increase with $k$, and
   their union over $k \in \mathbb{N}$ is $\mathbb{R}^n$.
2. Every bounded subset $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]) has $\lambda_n^*(E) < +\infty$; a bounded
   Lebesgue measurable set therefore has finite measure, and every compact
   subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is Lebesgue measurable of finite measure.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let
$f_n,f : X \to \mathbb R$ be measurable with $f_n,f \in L^1(\mu)$. If $f_n \to f$
in $L^1(\mu)$, then $f_n \to f$ in measure.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let
$f_n,f : X \to \mathbb R$ be measurable. If $f_n \to f$ in measure, then there
is a strictly increasing sequence $(n_k)_{k \ge 0}$ of natural numbers such
that $f_{n_k} \to f$ $\mu$-almost everywhere.

The construction below uses the **least** admissible index at each stage, so no
choice principle is spent.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

derivations.claim: Fix a compact space-time rectangle $Q$ and a fixed compact enlargement $Q'$ containing $Q$ and every spatial translate $Q+d_k$ for all sufficiently large $k$. Choose local bounds $H,M$ so that $0\le h_k\le H$ and $|u_k|\le M$ on $Q'$. Strong local $L^1$ convergence implies the same bounds for $h,u$ almost everywhere on $Q'$: by [F4], a subsequence converges almost everywhere there, and its pointwise limit inherits the bounds. By [F3], multiplying $h,u$ by the indicator of $Q'$ therefore gives $L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ functions. Applying [F2] to these cutoffs shows $h(\cdot+d_k,\cdot)\to h$ and $u(\cdot+d_k,\cdot)\to u$ in $L^1(Q)$. Strong local convergence on $Q'$ and the triangle inequality then show $h_k(\cdot+d_k,\cdot)\to h$ and $u_k(\cdot+d_k,\cdot)\to u$ in $L^1(Q)$ as well.

Let $L$ be a Lipschitz constant for $b$ on the spatial enlargement. Hydrostatic clipping changes either adjacent depth by at most $Ld_k$, so both reconstructed depths converge in measure on $Q$ to $h$. A reconstructed velocity differs from the cell velocity only when a positive cell is clipped to zero; that can occur only where $0<h_k\le Ld_k$. Take any subsequence. By [F4], it has a further subsequence on which the shifted depths and velocities converge almost everywhere on $Q$. Where the limit depth is positive there is eventually no clipping; where the limit depth is zero, the limit velocity is zero and the bounded cell velocities tend to zero. Thus the velocity-reset error tends to zero almost everywhere on this further subsequence. Its absolute value is bounded by $2M$ on $Q$, so [F3] and [F5] give convergence to zero in $L^1(Q)$ on that further subsequence. Since every subsequence has such a further subsequence, the subsequence criterion for convergence of real sequences shows that the full reset error tends to zero in $L^1(Q)$. Hence both reconstructed primitive states converge in measure to $(h,u)$ on $Q$.

At a wet limit state $h>0$, the two face inputs tend to the same $(h,hu)$; the left, middle and right HLL branches all tend to $F(h,hu)$, and the formulas agree at the branch boundaries. At a dry limit state, $h=0$ and $u=0$, so both reconstructed fluxes and both speeds tend to zero. In the middle branch write $\alpha=a_R$, $\beta=-a_L$; its equivalent formula is $\widehat F=(\alpha F_L^*+\beta F_R^*)/(\alpha+\beta)-[\alpha\beta/(\alpha+\beta)](U_R^*-U_L^*)$. Here $\alpha\beta/(\alpha+\beta)\le\max(\alpha,\beta)$, which tends to zero at the dry state, while $F_L^*,F_R^*,U_L^*,U_R^*$ tend to zero. The outer branches also tend to zero. Thus along each almost-everywhere convergent further subsequence from step 2.1, the HLL flux tends almost everywhere to $F(h,hu)$. The same equivalent formula and $\alpha,\beta\le M+\sqrt{gH}$ give a uniform bound on the fluxes on $Q$.

Apply [F4] to an arbitrary subsequence of the face-flux sequence to obtain a further subsequence with almost-everywhere convergence; step 3.1 gives its limit and uniform bound. Since $Q$ has finite measure by [F3], [F5] yields $L^1(Q)$ convergence along that further subsequence. If the full sequence failed to converge in $L^1(Q)$, some subsequence would stay a fixed positive distance from the limit, contradicting the further-subsequence conclusion. Therefore $\mathcal F_k\to F(h,hu)$ in $L^1(Q)$. As $Q$ was arbitrary, the convergence is local.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $d,\tau>0$, $I_i=[id,(i+1)d)$, $t_n=n\tau$, and $J_n=[t_n,t_{n+1})$. Suppose vector states and shared face fluxes satisfy
$$d(U_i^{n+1}-U_i^n)+\tau(\widehat F_{i+1/2}^n-\widehat F_{i-1/2}^n)=d\tau S_i^n$$
as in [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]]. For $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R\times(-\infty,T);\mathbb R^2)$ define the space-time cell average
$$\Phi_i^n=\frac1{d\tau}\int_{J_n}\int_{I_i}\varphi(x,t)\,dx\,dt.$$
Choose $N$ such that $\varphi$ vanishes for $t\ge t_{N-1}$. Then
$$\sum_i d\,U_i^0\cdot\Phi_i^0+\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\sum_i d\,U_i^n\cdot(\Phi_i^n-\Phi_i^{n-1})+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\sum_i\tau\,\widehat F_{i+1/2}^n\cdot(\Phi_{i+1}^n-\Phi_i^n)+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\sum_i d\tau\,S_i^n\cdot\Phi_i^n=0.$$
Every sum is finite because the test is compactly supported.

Let $b\in C^2(\mathbb R)$, let the uniform cell width be $d>0$, let $x_i$ be the center of cell $i$, and let $0\le h_i^n\le H$ on a fixed compact space-time cylinder. Set $b_i=b(x_i)$, $\delta_{i,+}=(b(x_i+d)-b(x_i))_+$, and $\delta_{i,-}=(b(x_i-d)-b(x_i))_+$. For the source term $S_i^n$ in [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]],
$$S_i^n=\left(0,\frac{g}{2d}\left((h_i^n-\delta_{i,+})_+^2-(h_i^n-\delta_{i,-})_+^2\right)\right),$$
there is a constant $C$ depending only on the compact interval, $b$, $g$, and $H$ such that
$$\left|S_i^{(2)}+g h_i b'(x_i)\right|\le C d.$$
For time slabs $J_n=[n\tau,(n+1)\tau)$, define the piecewise-constant source reconstruction $\mathcal S_d(x,t)=S_i^n$ on $[x_i-d/2,x_i+d/2)\times J_n$. Consequently, if the corresponding piecewise-constant depth reconstructions $h_d$ converge strongly in $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R\times(0,T))$ to $h$ and are locally uniformly bounded, then $\mathcal S_d\to(0,-ghb')$ strongly in $L^1_{\rm loc}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $d_k,\tau_k>0$ tend to zero, set $I_i^k=[id_k,(i+1)d_k)$, $x_i^k=(i+\tfrac12)d_k$, $t_n^k=n\tau_k$, and $J_n^k=[t_n^k,t_{n+1}^k)$, and let $b\in C^1(\mathbb R)$ be locally Lipschitz. On each cell-time slab let $h_k,u_k$ be piecewise constant, with $h_k\ge0$, $u_k=0$ when $h_k=0$, and $m_k=h_ku_k$. Suppose $h_k\to h$ and $u_k\to u$ strongly in $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R\times(0,T))$, $u=0$ almost everywhere where $h=0$, and $h_k,|u_k|$ are locally uniformly bounded. Let $\mathcal F_k(x,t)=\widehat F_{i+1/2}^{k,n}$ for $(x,t)\in I_i^k\times J_n^k$, with face flux from [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]] and bed samples $b(x_i^k)$. Then
$$\mathcal F_k\longrightarrow F(h,hu)\quad\text{strongly in }L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R\times(0,T)).$$
The primitive-velocity convergence and uniform velocity bound are included because the assigned wave-speed formula uses $m/h$ on wet states, which is not continuous at a dry state as a function of $(h,m)$ alone.

Let $h_k\ge0$ almost everywhere on $\mathbb R\times(0,T)$ and suppose $h_k\to h$ strongly in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Let $u$ be measurable, put $m=hu$ almost everywhere, and suppose $u=0$ almost everywhere on $\{h=0\}$. Then $U=(h,m)$ belongs to the admissible state set $K$ from [[def-pe05-shallow-water-balance-law]] almost everywhere. Also, let initial reconstructions $U_k^0=(h_k^0,m_k^0)\in K$ satisfy $m_k^0=h_k^0u_k^0$, $u_k^0=0$ where $h_k^0=0$, and $|u_k^0|\le M_Q$ on each compact spatial interval $Q$ for a constant $M_Q$ independent of $k$. If $U_k^0\to U_0=(h_0,m_0)$ strongly in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R)$, then $U_0\in K$ almost everywhere.

derivations.claim: By [F5], applied to the nonnegative bulk and initial depths, the strong local convergences, $m=hu$, the dry-velocity convention and the local initial velocity bound, both $U$ and $U_0$ belong to $K$ almost everywhere. Thus $F(U)$ in the weak formulation is defined.

Fix $\varphi$ and choose $N_k$ so that $\varphi$ vanishes for $t\ge t_{N_k-1}^k$ for all sufficiently large $k$. Apply [F2] to the actual states, shared face fluxes and source terms of the scheme; its exact finite sum is zero for each such $k$.

The initial term in [F2] tends to $\int_{\mathbb R}U_0(x)\cdot\varphi(x,0)\,dx$. Indeed, on each cell-time slab touching $t=0$, the averaged test differs from $\varphi(x,0)$ by at most $C_\varphi(d_k+\tau_k)$, and the uniform state bound including the initial layer makes the sum of these quadrature errors tend to zero on the fixed compact support. The initial reconstruction convergence then gives the claimed limit.

The time-difference sum in [F2] differs from $\int_0^T\int \mathcal U_k\cdot\varphi_t$ by $O(\tau_k)$. Taylor's formula in time makes each difference of adjacent cell-time test averages equal to the integral of $\varphi_t$ over the current slab, up to $C_\varphi\tau_k^2$ after spatial averaging; the uniform state bound and the $O(d_k^{-1}\tau_k^{-1})$ cells/slabs meeting the support give total error $O(\tau_k)$. The omitted initial-slab integral is also $O(\tau_k)$.

The face-flux sum in [F2] differs from $\int_0^T\int\mathcal F_k\cdot\varphi_x$ by $O(d_k)$. For each cell, the difference of adjacent test averages is the spatial average of $\int_0^{d_k}\varphi_x(x+s,t)\,ds$; replacing this average by $\varphi_x(x,t)$ has error at most $C_\varphi d_k^2\tau_k$ per cell-time slab. The local HLL flux bound and the number of cells/slabs meeting the support give the stated total error. The source sum in [F2] is exactly $\int_0^T\int\mathcal S_k\cdot\varphi$ because $\mathcal S_k$ is constant on each slab.

Strong local $L^1$ convergence gives $\int\mathcal U_k\cdot\varphi_t\to\int U\cdot\varphi_t$. By [F4], the face term tends to $\int F(U)\cdot\varphi_x$, and by [F3], the source term tends to $\int(0,-ghb_x)\cdot\varphi$. Step 1.3 supplies the initial term, while steps 1.4–1.5 identify the limits of the discrete sums; step 1.2 supplies the exact discrete identity and step 1.1 its state admissibility. Passing to the limit proves the displayed weak formulation.

Fix gravity $g>0$ and a stationary bed $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$. A shallow-water state is a pair $U=(h,m)$ with depth $h\ge0$ and momentum $m\in\mathbb R$. Its admissible wet/dry state set is
$$K=\{(h,m):h>0,\ m\in\mathbb R\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.$$
For $U\in K$, define velocity by $u=m/h$ when $h>0$ and $u=0$ when $h=0$. Thus a dry state has both $h=0$ and $m=0$. Define the free surface by $\eta=h+b$ and the physical flux by
$$F(U)=\begin{cases}(m,\ m^2/h+gh^2/2),&h>0,\\(0,0),&U=(0,0).\end{cases}$$
For a continuously differentiable bed, the one-dimensional shallow-water balance law is
$$U_t+\partial_xF(U)=(0,-gh\,b_x).$$
The source is evaluated as zero at a dry state.

A discrete lake-at-rest profile with level $\eta_0$ has $m_i=0$ and $h_i+b_i=\eta_0$ in every wet cell; cells with $h_i=0$ are dry and satisfy $b_i\ge\eta_0$.

For any discrete bed values, the update of [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]] leaves every lake-at-rest profile of [[def-pe05-shallow-water-balance-law]] unchanged, including a wet/dry shoreline with dry cells above the free-surface level.

derivations.claim: The data are admissible by [F1]. The four face maxima, including the periodic face between cells $4$ and $0$, are $(1,2,2,1,0)$, so the paired reconstructed depths are respectively $(1,1)$, $(0,0)$, $(0,0)$, $(1,1)$, and $(2,2)$. All reconstructed velocities are zero.

At these equal states the common HLL fluxes are $(0,1/2)$, $(0,0)$, $(0,0)$, $(0,1/2)$ and $(0,2)$. Adding the one-sided pressure corrections in [F2] makes the two corrected fluxes adjacent to each cell both equal $(0,h_i^2/2)$: the five cell pressures are $2,1/2,0,1/2,2$.

Each cell therefore has zero corrected-flux difference in the update, so every state is unchanged, including the dry crest. This verifies the exact lake-at-rest preservation in [F3] for this finite wet/dry example.

Let $N\ge1$ cells form a finite chain, with two admissible ghost states used only to define the boundary faces, or let the cells be periodic. Apply one step of [[def-pe05-hydrostatic-hll-scheme]] to states in $K$ from [[def-pe05-shallow-water-balance-law]]. If
$$\lambda\big(a_{R,i+1/2}-a_{L,i-1/2}\big)\le1\quad(1\le i\le N),$$
then each updated state remains in $K$. The depth is nonnegative; if it is zero then the momentum is zero. On a finite chain the total water changes by the net boundary discharge, and on a periodic mesh total water is conserved.

derivations.claim: At every wet/wet face the states agree at $(1,0)$, the speeds are $(-1,1)$, and the HLL flux is $(0,1/2)$. At every dry/dry face the speeds and flux are zero. At the unique wet/dry face, $F_L=(0,1/2)$, $F_R=(0,0)$, $U_R-U_L=(-1,0)$ and $a_La_R=-1$, so the middle formula in [F1] gives $\widehat F=(1/2,1/4)$.

For a wet cell adjacent to the front the outgoing-speed sum is $1+1=2$, so $\lambda$ times that sum is $1$; for the first dry cell it is $1+0=1$, so the product is $1/2$; all other cells have either the wet/wet value $1$ or the dry/dry value $0$ on each side, and satisfy the same bound. Thus every cell meets [F2].

The wet cell $i=0$ has left flux $(0,1/2)$ and right flux $(1/2,1/4)$, hence $U_0^1=(1,0)-\tfrac12((1/2,1/4)-(0,1/2))=(3/4,1/8)$. The dry cell $i=1$ has left flux $(1/2,1/4)$ and right flux $(0,0)$, hence $U_1^1=(0,0)-\tfrac12((0,0)-(1/2,1/4))=(1/4,1/8)$. Both depths are positive, and their sum remains $1$, so the front wets the adjacent dry cell without losing water.
